answers.recommendation: Overall: mostly sound, with six real problems listed as items 6 to 11 below. Checks that passed: the CH10-12 span rows parse; Nagoji, Varma and Padmini have no gaps or overlaps in chapters 10, 11 and 12; the boots and barefoot splits in chapter 10 (1.4 to 2.5 and 9.1) and chapter 12 (2 to 3) match the scripts; the 10 @9.4 and 11 @21.3 forearm rows match the scripts; the Varma headwear rows match each scene; and the Padmini cotton-sari row is right for chapters 10 and 11. The bible, the sidecars and the cast files contain no em or en dashes. The dry-run packages ending -e match the current sidecars byte for byte, and I read those prompts. The scoped-rule edit to 'Non-Maratha raiders' and rivals' banners' is correct and needed: chapter 12 panels 4.4 (travancore_camp) and 8.3 (carnatic) draw saffron Maratha pennants, and the old wording would have contradicted them. Renaming the entry to 'Chanda Sahib of Arcot' is harmless: the pipeline still finds his entry.

Remove the temple priest from 10.1.5. The script notes say no V13 temple-priest sheet is attached anywhere in chapter 10, because the officiant is too small to identify and the sheet risks putting his face on Ramayyan. At the moment the dry-run prompt lists 'Temple priest face' among PEOPLE, attaches his sheet as image 3, and prints a LOOKS line for him. Removing him does not break the cast check: the only name it looks for is the literal key 'temple_priest', so the word 'priest' in the description does not trigger it. Ramayyan's MUST MATCH line ('never the officiating priest's face') stays.

answers.recommendation: Take Ramayyan out of the cast for 10.8.2 and mark him as not shown. The panel is a gallop through bamboo; only his hand appears, in an inset. Right now the prompt says 'PEOPLE: Nagoji, Ramayyan Dalawa', attaches his full sheet and his LOOKS line, which invites a whole Ramayyan among the riders. Turning sheets off for the panel would also drop Nagoji's sheet, and he leads the charge. With Ramayyan as not shown, the cast check is still satisfied, Nagoji keeps his sheet, and the hand is described on its own.
